scope: Corollary 7.1 (Degraded two-receiver pure-loss broadcast capacity) of the manuscript “The entropy photon-number inequality” (preprints/The-entropy-photon-number-inequality-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 273 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d826f8ebe1859641), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 26-27. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let 0 ≤ N̄ < ∞, 0 ≤ ηC < ηB, and ηB + ηC ≤ 1. The classical capacity region for the channel and coding model above, with rates 26 in nats per use, is the closed convex hull of the nonnegative pairs (RB, RC) satisfying, for some 0 ≤ β ≤ 1, RB ≤ g(ηBβN̄), RC ≤ g(ηCN̄) − g(ηCβN̄), (7.2) where g is the natural-log function in (1.1).
